VibePascal v59 -- aarch64-darwin native compiler (runs on Apple Silicon macOS).
A COM interface function-result temp is released at the end of its statement.

an existing aarch64-darwin unit set stays valid and the utility binaries are
unchanged and not re-shipped.

WHAT CHANGED IN v59 -- A COM INTERFACE TEMP DIES WITH ITS STATEMENT
  A function that returns a COM interface, called where its result is never
  stored in a variable ("Giver.Need.o.DoWork;"), leaves the reference in a
  hidden temp.  Up to v58 that temp was released only when the ROUTINE exited
  (or when the compiler happened to recycle the slot), so the object stayed
  checked out long past its line -- a holder that should have handed its object
  back at the semicolon kept it until the end of the procedure.  v59 releases it
  at the end of the source statement that produced it, the way Delphi does.

  Two commits carry it, and the second one is why the first did not ship alone:

    55e687f581  (GOD, 2026-09-16)  the mechanism.  A temp knows it holds a COM
                interface (tgobj), a slot still holding one is never recycled
                under a second result in the same statement, and tcgblocknode
                releases the statement's temps after every statement of a
                begin..end block.

    5c89c538b8  (Otto, 2026-09-17)  three holes measured on that build with
                the two matrices added in tests/test/ (tintfstmttemp1.pp, 32
                corners; tintfstmttemp2.pp, 28 corners), closed before anything
                shipped:
                  * a statement nested inside another -- the body of a
                    with/if/while/case whose EXPRESSION produced the temp --
                    released its parent's temp.  `with Giver.Need.o do begin
                    A; B end` ran B on a freed object (measured: the owner's
                    refcount hit zero after A).  Each temp now records which
                    source statement allocated it and a statement releases
                    only its own, never an enclosing one's.
                  * exit, break, continue, goto and raise LEAKED the temp for
                    good: the routine-exit sweep had been trimmed to skip
                    temps whose statement-end release existed, and those
                    escapes never reach that release.  Measured: every one of
                    them leaked exactly one object.  The sweep covers every
                    managed temp again; a slot that was already released is
                    nil and costs one compare, one that was abandoned is
                    released at routine exit, and nothing is released twice.
                  * repeat..until bodies, try/finally/except bodies and
                    case-else lists kept the old routine-exit lifetime, because
                    only begin..end had been marked as a source statement list.

  What does NOT change: an interface stored in a variable, field, array or
  Result lives exactly as long as it always did.  Two results used in one
  statement are both alive until that statement ends.  A temp produced by an
  if/while condition, a case selector or a with expression stays alive through
  the branch, the loop body or the with block and is released when that
  statement ends.

  COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change
  (the unit files' own header/version are untouched), so every existing unit
  set for this target stays valid and does not need rebuilding.  Code compiled
  by v59 simply releases these temps sooner.

HOW THE FIX WAS PROVEN, ON THE SOURCE EVERY TARGET IS BUILT FROM
  * tests/test/tintfstmttemp1.pp and tintfstmttemp2.pp, 60 self-checking
    corners in all (free proc, method, nested proc, main body, if/for/while/
    repeat/with bodies, two temps in one statement, a temp passed as a
    parameter, a stored interface, exit/break/continue/goto/raise mid-
    statement, a nested block under a with/if/while/case temp, try/finally/
    except/on/case-else bodies, an unentered block, and destroyed == created
    at the end): 60/60 on this source at -O- and -O2.  The same programs score
    35 failures on v58 (everything released at routine exit, nothing leaked,
    nothing freed early) and 31 on the 55e687f581 build (3 leaked objects, 4
    use-after-free corners, 6 statement lists left on the old lifetime) -- so
    the harness fails in both directions and a pass means something.
  * 1983-test corpus A/B against the PUBLISHED v58 x86_64-linux compiler:
    1983 SAME, 0 DIFF (compile status and run exit code per test).
  * self-host fixpoint on x86_64-linux: stage 2 == stage 3 byte-identical.
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh, the v57/v58 reader fixes are still in:
    25/25 offsets clean on x86_64-linux, i386-linux, aarch64-linux and
    arm-linux with the host-executable compilers.
  * dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh: x86_64-linux 147/147, i386-linux 146/146,
    aarch64-linux 144/144, arm-linux 143/143 packages load clean, zero
    recompiles.

HOW FAR THE VERIFICATION GOES ON THIS TARGET -- READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING IT
  THIS BINARY HAS NEVER BEEN EXECUTED.  The build host is x86_64-linux, there is
  no macOS on it, and no packaged emulator on this box runs a Mach-O.  That was
  equally true of every darwin binary before it; it is not a new gap, but it is
  a real one.

  What IS established:
    - Format and architecture checked with file(1) on the exact bytes in this
      tarball (Mach-O 64-bit, flags NOUNDEFS/DYLDLINK/TWOLEVEL/PIE).
    - The build really recompiled the patched code rather than relinking stale
      units: the per-target unit dir was wiped first and the five changed
      units (tgobj, hlcgobj, ncgbas, nbas, pstatmnt) plus version were written
      fresh; the unit COUNT is asserted, never the hash.
    - The fix is compiled in, by a SINGLE-AXIS Mach-O section triage: the v58
      source commit and the v59 source commit were each cross-built HERE,
      TODAY, with the same host compiler, the same RTL units and the same
      flags, and only then compared (numbers below).  The control that makes
      the delta a source measurement and not build noise is that the v58
      rebuild reproduces the v58 binary shipped on 2026-09-11 section for
      section.
    - The BEHAVIOUR of this source was proven by EXECUTION on this host, on the
      SAME CPU: the 60-corner lifetime matrices compiled and ran clean through
      the Linux-hosted compiler for this CPU (see HOW THE FIX WAS PROVEN).  The
      temp-lifetime change lives in CPU-independent code (tgobj, hlcgobj,
      ncgbas, the parser), so those runs are evidence about the source this
      binary was built from -- and only that.

  What is NOT established: that this binary starts, compiles or links on a Mac.
  If you have a macOS box, the one number worth sending back is the exit code of
  the compiler run with -iV (expect 0, printing 3.3.1) -- it needs no SDK and
  no unit set.  An unsigned arm64 binary is KILLED by Apple Silicon macOS
  (Killed: 9) as a policy result, not a compiler verdict; codesign -f -s - it
  and retry.

AD-HOC SIGNING CHANGES THIS HASH -- A MISMATCH IS NOT CORRUPTION
  Every md5/sha256 above describes the binary AS STAGED, UNSIGNED.  Darwin
  packaging in Lazarus build-release.sh ad-hoc signs every bundled Mach-O with
  rcodesign, and the compiler is hard-linked into the .app, so the signature
  rewrites the top-level copy too.  A signature appends bytes and changes the
  hash, so the number above CANNOT match the file inside a Lazarus darwin
  tarball.  The predicted AS-SHIPPED digests below are a CROSS-CHECK, not the
  authority: build-release.sh stamps an "AS SHIPPED IN THIS TARBALL" block
  computed after packaging, and that block wins if the two disagree.  The
  prediction procedure was validated in the same run against known answers:
  signing the v58 compilers under their shipped names reproduces their
  documented digests exactly (ppcx64 9393168 / 3c4caf87a0167b016a615579aef40fe7,
  ppca64 7338624 / b49919f66d9eee4f06fe6fff8f137c04).

  Section triage, arm64 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.2-size -m):
    v58 shipped 2026-09-11        __TEXT,__text 3829348   __DATA_CONST,__const 964384   7333151 bytes
    v58 source rebuilt today      __TEXT,__text 3829348   __DATA_CONST,__const 964384   7333153 bytes
                                  (every section size identical; 56680 bytes of
                                  linker metadata / __LINKEDIT packing move between
                                  runs on arm64, as they did for v55, v56 and v58,
                                  which is why SECTIONS are the instrument here and
                                  the file hash is not)
    v59 (this binary)             __TEXT,__text 3830180   __DATA_CONST,__const 964496   7333274 bytes
    delta v58 -> v59              __text +832, __const +112: the fix.

  Predicted AS-SHIPPED digests, if this binary is signed with no other mutation:
    ppca64   7338752 bytes
      md5    ab3d20b8ea24b56a291dc23c82510528
      sha256 ac1ef254543e2e97b907d51f819fbbb4c0e748f1429b24b8cb65f6086530deb3
  This binary is insensitive to the filename its signature is computed under
  (its linker embedded a Mach-O identifier); its Intel twin is not.
